Final message max 170 words: head SHA, per item CONFIRMED (failing test)/refuted/dismissed, blockers. Cap 120 tool calls; never ask questions. Every fix keeps the ledger model (one source of truth) and must not cause new classes of finding: grep the sibling sites and add parity tests.

THE REVIEW (verify each with a failing test on bd16ed31 first):
(1) PERF, wall time matters most: while any walk stays unread, a component is never memoized, `grow` runs on every request and `inherit_memos` discards EVERY memo in the session (lazy.rs ~1306: `any_unread()`): one permanently unreadable `.d.ts` (EACCES) makes every request cost two resolutions plus a layer extension, grows the layer chain toward MAX_CHAIN_DEPTH and regresses first-answer latency for the whole session, including components that never touch the bad file. Fix: (a) `inherit_memos` drops only memos of components whose transitive demands include a Failed ledger entry (the ledger already marks walk nodes), keeping all others; (b) a persistently failing path is retried on a backoff (mirror the checker side's `DEGRADED_RETRY`, injectable clock/counter, never wall time in tests) or until the file's mtime/size changes or an edit event arrives, so repeated requests for a component behind a failed read do not redo `grow` each time. Tests: exact counts of `grow`/resolutions across N requests with one permanently unreadable file (unrelated components: zero extra work and memos kept; affected component: at most one retry within the backoff; after the file is readable and the backoff passes or an edit arrives: the full answer equals cold). Report the request cost before/after. (2) An outcome with no entry for the component (a run past the heap budget, or a skipped target) is still kept as `Settled::Answered(Answered{component: None..})` and cached; a heap-budget run (Warning diagnostic, no component or fallback) then sticks until a file changes even after memory pressure is gone. Round 2 made `unavailable` an explicit marker so a real empty answer is not mistaken for an outage; the question now is what a BUDGET-EXCEEDED or SKIPPED run is. Inspect how the semantic crate reports over-budget and skipped targets (diagnostic codes/severities in crates/semantic): if the run is a budget or resource failure (not a verdict about this component), mark it transient with the same explicit-marker approach (set where the budget decision is made, never inferred from absence) so it is not cached or stored and is retried on the backoff; a target the pass legitimately skips (not part of the program, not a component) stays a kept answer. Test both with exact assertions; if the codes make the distinction impossible, say exactly why in the PR body. (3) A rejected `module_exports` (lib.rs ~815) is marked transient but keeps the reason 'not part of the checker's program' and drops the rejection message: every other Rejected site says `the checker rejected a request: {message}`; carry the message and do not state a verdict. Test the exact diagnostic text. (4) The cold-load index is written only when no read failed (`!loader.ledger.any_failed()`, dependency_types.rs ~1384), so one persistently unreadable file disables index learning for every later cold load (a cost the fewer-fs-calls work removed): persist the entries whose walks are COMPLETE (not marked in the ledger) and skip only the incomplete ones. Test: a package with one unreadable file and several complete walks: the index contains exactly the complete walks, a second cold run uses them (assert the fs-call/probe count drops) and equals the cold answer. (5) Add the missing test the mutation run found: within ONE load, a failed read of F followed by a successful read of F through another path keeps F Failed (the answers derived from the failed read are incomplete): assert it, and in the PR body state this is deliberate (the cost is one skipped index entry and a warning until the next load re-reads it). DISMISS with a one-line reason each in the PR body (no code change): (6) the removed once-per-session warning: each degraded answer carries the warning tagged `affects=[that component]`, so the N warnings are N true statements, one per degraded component, and the output dedups identical ones; (7) the findings about code on main or other open PRs, listed so they are tracked, not dropped: `reroot` not releasing snapshots when it fails part-way (#515), `BatchAnswers` slot memory (#513), `member_name` applied only to object fields (#519), the flights walk-0 default (#513/#526): say they are not in this PR's diff and are follow-ups. 1	## What
2	
3	Two shared-state defects where a transient failure was stored as an answer. Both confirmed by tests that fail on `origin/main` (`f4a88f93`).
4	
5	**1. A checker outage was kept as the component's answer** (`crates/core/src/pipeline/semantic_hook.rs`; audit shared-state hit 1, semantic-wire hit 1).
6	
7	- Cause: `read_outcome` turned an outcome with no component and no fallback (`SemanticOutcome::unavailable`: timeout, crash, checker not running) into `Answered { component: None, diagnostics: [] }`, and `ask` inserted every `Answered` into `cache.answers`. The warning went to a once-per-session `warned` flag. Every later request until a source edit got structural props, no diagnostic, `awaits_checker` false.
8	- Fix: the notion is a type. `Settled` gains `Degraded(Vec<Diagnostic>)`; `read_outcome` returns it for an outcome that answers nothing. `ask` inserts only `Settled::Answered`. `refine` attaches a degraded request's diagnostics (each with `affects` = the component) to every answer it affects. The `warned` flag is gone. The next request asks the checker again.
9	- `awaits_checker` stays false on a degraded answer: a checker that stays down (`MAX_RESTARTS`, could not start) answers at once, so a host that re-asked on `awaits_checker` would loop. Not caching is what makes the next request ask again.
10	
11	**2. A failed dependency read was persisted as "not exported"** (`crates/core/src/dependency_types.rs`; audit shared-state hit 4).
12	
13	- Cause: `Loader::read` returned `None` on an I/O error, the `parsed` `OnceLock` stored `None`, `find_export_uncached` returned `None` without `cut`, the miss was cached, `learn`ed and written by `write_index` as `(module, name, None)`. Later runs trusted it while `package.json` was unchanged.
14	- Fix:
15	  - `read_text` returns `Err(Unreadable)` for a file that exists but cannot be read (still reports the Warning diagnostic once, as before). `parse_source` returns `Result<Option<_>, Unreadable>` and does not initialize the `parsed` cell on a failed read, so the next caller reads again.
16	  - `find_export_uncached` treats `Unreadable` as a cut (the cycle-cut mechanism): the miss is returned but neither kept, `learn`ed nor persisted.
17	  - The layer keeps only initialized `parsed` cells (`load`), so a session's next revision reads the file again instead of finding `None` in its parent.
18	  - `write_index` writes nothing when any dependency read failed in the run: an augmentation search's answer can hold the failure as an absence.
19	
20	Invariant: a failure to read or to ask is unknown, never absence; nothing derived from it enters a cache, a layer or the index.
21	
22	## Evidence
23	
24	Tests (each fails on `origin/main`, passes here):
25	
26	- `semantic_hook::a_request_the_checker_did_not_answer_is_asked_again_and_answered`: a fake provider returns `SemanticOutcome::unavailable(..)` for the first request, `finds_size` for the second. Request 2 carries `["label", "size"]`, equal (props and diagnostics) to a fresh session that never saw the outage. Base: `["label"]`.
27	- `semantic_hook::an_unavailable_checker_warns_on_every_answer_it_affects_and_never_fails_a_request` (replaces `..._warns_once_per_session_...`): Button, Card, Button again each carry one `SemanticBackend` Warning with `affects` = that key; 3 provider requests. Base: Card had none.
28	- `semantic_join::an_unavailable_checker_is_reported_to_the_story_that_joined_the_request_and_to_every_later_one` (was `..._reported_once_...`): warnings (1, 1). Base: (1, 0).
29	- `dependency_types::tests::an_export_in_a_file_that_could_not_be_read_is_found_on_the_next_run` (unix, `chmod 000` then restore): the unreadable run reports one Warning for the file; a session extension of that layer (demand from another directory) finds the export; the next cold run with the cache on finds it, equal to the oracle run with `use_cache: false`. Base: `(false, Some(NotExported))`.
30	- `dependency_types::augmentation_tests::a_file_an_augmentation_search_could_not_read_is_searched_again_on_the_next_run`: next run's `augmenters_of(reexp)` = `[inner/index.d.ts]`, equal to the cache-off oracle. Base: `[]`.
31	
32	Mutation proof (each guard removed, a test fails):
33	
34	- drop `*cut = true` on `Unreadable` -> `an_export_in_a_file_that_could_not_be_read_is_found_on_the_next_run` fails.
35	- drop the `write_index` gate -> `a_file_an_augmentation_search_could_not_read_is_searched_again_on_the_next_run` fails.
36	- keep uninitialized `parsed` cells in the layer as `None` -> `an_export_in_a_file_that_could_not_be_read_is_found_on_the_next_run` fails.
37	
38	Gates (exit codes):
39	
40	- `just lint doc-check machete typos`: exit 0.
41	- `cargo nextest run --workspace --no-fail-fast` (sandbox off): exit 0, 1745 passed, 3 skipped.
42	- `just test-checker-lane` (no `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`): exit 0.
43	- `gate_harness determinism --tsc built-in` on `gate_fixtures.mjs` output in scratch: exit 0, 150 components, 9 variants (1/2/4 threads, reversed), all `equalsFirst`, 148 answered by the checker.
44	- `gate_harness memory --tsc built-in`: exit 0, 650 edits, 650 answered by the checker, 0 stale, `finalEqualsFresh`, peak RSS 361 MiB.
45	- Output vs a release build of `origin/main` (`extract --src <dir> --json --quiet --no-cache`, JSON parsed, `stats` dropped): identical on mantine `@mantine/core/src` (348 components) and chakra-ui `packages/react/src` (629 components). Neither run had a `SEMANTIC_BACKEND` diagnostic with severity other than info (checked by code and severity), so no run was dropped.
46	- Load during the gates: 1-minute average 19-69 on a shared machine; no timing was taken.
47	
48	Sweep, other places that keep an outcome or a read (not changed here, for the next fix to use the `Degraded`/`Unreadable` notion):
49	
50	- `crates/semantic/src/kept.rs:334` `save`: skips an outcome with diagnostics, so an `unavailable` one is not kept, but an outcome whose fallbacks came from `CallError::Rejected` (a tsrs panic, `STOPPED`, a decode error) has no diagnostics and is saved to the kept-answer file. Called from `lib.rs:216-229` (`resolve_cached`).
51	- `crates/semantic/src/lib.rs:838` turns `CallError::Rejected` (including `checker.rs:568` `STOPPED` and a caught panic) into a `SemanticFallback`. The hook caches a fallback as an answer, so a component asked while the checker panicked keeps that Info fallback until an edit. Fix belongs there (or in `on_demand.rs::answer` when `!backend.is_alive()` after the request): emit no fallback for a rejection caused by a stopped checker, so the outcome reads as degraded. Not done here: `lib.rs` is another worker's, and no test can inject a panicking built-in backend into `OnDemand` without a new seam.
52	- `dependency_types.rs` `Loader::demand` -> `unresolved_cause_in` (`self.parse(module)?`): an unreadable module yields `NotExported` in `unresolved`, which the layer keeps, and the demand is in `demands`, so a session does not re-run that exact demand until the layer is rebuilt. Not persisted (`unresolved` is never written).
53	- `dependency_types.rs` `augmentation_scan` (`self.read(file)?`) and `find_augmenting_files`: an unreadable file is skipped and the module's augmenter list without it is kept in `augmenters` for the run and its layer. No longer persisted (the `write_index` gate).
54	- `load_declaration`, `load_augmentations`, the React path of `demand`, and the `named`/`react_files` passes in `load` use `parse` and skip an unreadable file without caching anything derived from it.
55	
56	## Round 2
57	
58	Review of `b70e8f38`, fixed at the class level. Each item has a test that fails without the fix (mutation proof below).
59	
60	**1. A failed read is a type every consumer must handle** (`crates/core/src/dependency_types.rs`). CONFIRMED (session path), PARTLY REFUTED (index path).
61	
62	- `Unreadable` is now `ReadFailed`. `Loader::read`, `parse`, `parse_source`, `augmentation_scan`, `find_augmenting_files`, `augmenting_files`, `find_export(_in, _uncached)`, `unresolved_cause(_in)`, `load_declaration`, `load_augmentations`, `module_demand` and the new `follow` return `Result<_, ReadFailed>`; the `.ok().flatten()` wrappers are gone, so a new consumer cannot drop it silently.
63	- Every consumer and its decision:
64	  - `parse_source`: the per-file cell holds the read's result, the failure included, for this load only; `load` keeps only `Ok` cells in the layer, so the next load reads the file again.
65	  - `find_export_in` / `find_export_uncached` (export walk, `export *` included): `Err` propagates; nothing on the walk is inserted in `exports` or `learn`ed.
66	  - `unresolved_cause_in`: `Err` propagates; no `NotExported` enters `unresolved`.
67	  - `follow` (React path, export path, module path): `Err` puts the demand key in `failed`; `load` leaves `failed` keys out of the layer's `demands`, so `missing` returns them and a session's next load follows them again.
68	  - `load_declaration` (claim): `Err` before any claim, so nothing enters `claimed`, `declaring` or `react_files`; the demand that called it is `failed`.
69	  - `augmentation_scan` (entry, React-mentioning and re-export-only files): one `ScanCell` per file holds the scan, the failure included, for this load; never in the layer.
70	  - `find_augmenting_files` / `augmenting_files`: `Err` propagates; the list is not inserted in `augmenters` or `augmenter_crossed`, so neither the layer nor the index holds it.
71	  - `module_demand`: the `(scope, specifier)` cell now holds the parsed augmenting files or `ReadFailed`, so every demand of the scope, not only the first, is `failed` alike.
72	  - `load` (`files` and `react_files` passes): read the cells a successful claim initialized; `Ok(Some)` only.
73	  - `resolve` (`resolutions`): does not call `read`; oxc_resolver stats files, so a resolution is not derived from a failed read. Kept; the table test asserts every resolution equals the oracle's.
74	- `DependencyLayer::degraded` = a read failed in this load or a layer below; `write_index` runs only when `!degraded`. Refuted part of the finding: `write_index` already ran only for a cold load (`previous == None`), so a child load never wrote the index on its parent's behalf; the marker is carried anyway. No test fails when the gate is removed, since nothing derived from a failed read reaches the loader's maps any more; it is defence in depth.
75	- `scan`'s `parse_source(file, Some(source)).ok().flatten()` could not hide a failure (it passes the text, so it never reads); it is now `?` like the rest.
76	
77	**2. A degraded answer is held as a short-lived refusal** (`crates/core/src/pipeline/semantic_hook.rs`). CONFIRMED.
78	
79	- `AnswerCache::degraded`: `(key, stamp) -> (when, diagnostics)`, separate from `answers`. `find` returns `Found::Degraded` within `DEGRADED_RETRY` (30 s): the structural props plus the same diagnostics, without asking the checker. After it, or after `invalidate` (any source change, which clears it), the next request asks again; a recovered checker's answer is kept as usual.
80	- The clock is a `Clock` field (`Instant::now`), replaced in the unit test.
81	- `awaits_checker` stays false on a degraded answer: it means "ask again and you get the checker's props", which is false for 30 s; the Warning (`degradedBy` in the addon) tells the host the answer is degraded. A host that polled on `awaits_checker` would spin for the whole retry.
82	
83	**3. Unavailability is a mark, not an absence** (`crates/core/src/types/semantic.rs`). CONFIRMED.
84	
85	- `SemanticOutcome::unavailable: Option<Unavailable>`; `Unavailable(())` has a private field, so only `SemanticOutcome::unavailable(..)` can set it. `read_outcome` decides from it alone; an outcome with no entry for the key (a skipped target, a run past its heap budget) is `Settled::Answered` and kept.
86	
87	**4. One read per file per load** (`parse_source`, `augmentation_scan`). CONFIRMED.
88	
89	- The read happens inside the cell's `get_or_init`; callers that meet wait for the first and get its result, a failed read included. A file both parsed and scanned by callers that meet can still be read once by each reader kind (as on `origin/main`).
90	
91	**5. A transient fallback is never kept** (`crates/core/src/types/semantic.rs`, `crates/semantic/src/lib.rs`, `crates/semantic/src/kept.rs`). CONFIRMED.
92	
93	- `SemanticFallback::transient: bool`. `lib.rs` `rejected_fallback_of` sets it for `CallError::Rejected` in `answer_file`, at both sites: a component's request (~838) and `module_exports` (~796, which also merged a rejection into "not part of the checker's program").
94	- `SemanticOutcome::is_degraded()` = unavailable or any transient fallback. `to_bytes` refuses a degraded outcome (its marks are not stored), so `kept::save` writes nothing for it; that is the one owner. The hook reads a transient fallback for the asked key as `Settled::Degraded`.
95	
96	Tests (each fails with its guard removed):
97	
98	- `dependency_types::tests::a_file_that_could_not_be_read_is_read_again_by_the_next_load_on_every_path`: rows `ExportWalk`, `Claim` (index answered the export, warm run first), `EntryScan`, `ReExportScan`, `AugmentingScan`; `chmod 000`, cache on. Per row: the file is reported, the layer is `degraded`, its answers differ from the oracle's, and the session's next load (`missing` demands over the layer) and the next cold run equal the oracle (cache off): followed, files loaded, unresolved reasons, resolutions, `reexp`'s augmenters.

Two shared-state defects where a transient failure was stored as an answer. Both confirmed by tests that fail on `origin/main` (`f4a88f93`).

**1. A checker outage was kept as the component's answer** (`crates/core/src/pipeline/semantic_hook.rs`; audit shared-state hit 1, semantic-wire hit 1).

- Cause: `read_outcome` turned an outcome with no component and no fallback (`SemanticOutcome::unavailable`: timeout, crash, checker not running) into `Answered { component: None, diagnostics: [] }`, and `ask` inserted every `Answered` into `cache.answers`. The warning went to a once-per-session `warned` flag. Every later request until a source edit got structural props, no diagnostic, `awaits_checker` false.
- Fix: the notion is a type. `Settled` gains `Degraded(Vec<Diagnostic>)`; `read_outcome` returns it for an outcome that answers nothing. `ask` inserts only `Settled::Answered`. `refine` attaches a degraded request's diagnostics (each with `affects` = the component) to every answer it affects. The `warned` flag is gone. The next request asks the checker again.
- `awaits_checker` stays false on a degraded answer: a checker that stays down (`MAX_RESTARTS`, could not start) answers at once, so a host that re-asked on `awaits_checker` would loop. Not caching is what makes the next request ask again.

**2. A failed dependency read was persisted as "not exported"** (`crates/core/src/dependency_types.rs`; audit shared-state hit 4).

- Cause: `Loader::read` returned `None` on an I/O error, the `parsed` `OnceLock` stored `None`, `find_export_uncached` returned `None` without `cut`, the miss was cached, `learn`ed and written by `write_index` as `(module, name, None)`. Later runs trusted it while `package.json` was unchanged.
- Fix:
  - `read_text` returns `Err(Unreadable)` for a file that exists but cannot be read (still reports the Warning diagnostic once, as before). `parse_source` returns `Result<Option<_>, Unreadable>` and does not initialize the `parsed` cell on a failed read, so the next caller reads again.
  - `find_export_uncached` treats `Unreadable` as a cut (the cycle-cut mechanism): the miss is returned but neither kept, `learn`ed nor persisted.
  - The layer keeps only initialized `parsed` cells (`load`), so a session's next revision reads the file again instead of finding `None` in its parent.
  - `write_index` writes nothing when any dependency read failed in the run: an augmentation search's answer can hold the failure as an absence.

Invariant: a failure to read or to ask is unknown, never absence; nothing derived from it enters a cache, a layer or the index.

Round 2 made a failed read abort the walk (`?`), so one unreadable file cost every answer the walk had already read or would read next; `origin/main` went on with the walk. **Artifacts**: PR body with `## What`, `## Evidence` (numbers, exit codes, what was diffed), `## Not verified`, last line the session url; the lead publishes it unedited. Final message <= 120 words: branch, head SHA (ls-remote verified), body path, blockers.

- Grammar sweep: list every syntax/type form the code can receive and show each is handled or declined (exhaustive match, or a generated test over the grammar with the checker/TS API as oracle). Generate over the grammar, not over past findings.

Three read-only audits on 2026-11-24 (reports committed on branch `docs/review-checklist` under `docs/audits/2026-11-24-*.md`) found that our recurring review findings are one root problem in three places: a DECISION is made from something that is not evidence. Extractor: a spelling (PascalCase callee, name lists, `contains("Component")`) or a raw expression. Wire boundary (crates/semantic): an ABSENT or defaulted field read as a value (`#[serde(default)]`, `unwrap_or(false)`, tsrs omits empty fields). Caches and sessions: a DEGRADED result (timeout, read failure, heap budget, nesting cut) stored as authoritative. The rules already exist in prose (CONTRIBUTING 'Before you push', ADR 0025-0028: by binding not spelling, one owner per decision, unknown unless proven, always emit a Diagnostic when degrading); nothing enforces them in code.

**Why:** reviews found 3 + 3 + 5 findings per PR in the same classes; each fix moved the problem (validating on a shared cache primed it the other way). Fixing per site does not converge.

**How to apply (direction, in this order):** (1) failing-first counter-example suites (extractor M10: every snippet in the audit becomes a row asserting exact output); (2) make invalid states unrepresentable: `ComponentEvidence` required to build a `ComponentMapping`, a typed `Peeled` (Transparent | Instantiated | Asserted) with one exhaustive match, `Known<T>` for decoded wire fields, a `Degraded` marker on outcomes that no cache or kept answer stores, `CallError::Contract` for undecodable responses with its own code; (3) one owner modules (`extractor/decide.rs`, `semantic/src/wire.rs` with one tsrs version-pin test, one `Memo` abstraction); (4) architecture tests (grep-based Rust tests, no new scripts) that fail on a catch-all arm or a name literal in a decision, `unwrap_or(false)` on wire values, text matching of messages, statics in non-test code; (5) determinism as a tested property: differential tests with separate state per consumer as oracle, session equals cold extract under random edit scripts. Amend ADR 0027/0026: 'a name is a candidate filter, never a verdict'. Related: [[diagnose-after-three-findings]], [[workers-run-full-lint-gate]].

On 2026-11-14 the user said they were "disappointed that you're not taking a step back to understand the patterns, consider the architecture and our models" after the Storybook live-upgrade PR (#462) collected 11 findings over 5 rounds that I routed one at a time as spot fixes. I had promised a model-based approach "if another finding appears" and still patched the next one.

**Why:** findings arrive serially from a reviewer that sees a slice each round; workers capped at 25-35 calls patch the symptom. The 11 findings shared four root causes: no explicit lifecycle model (state scattered across flags keyed by the wrong dimension: component instead of component+revision+key+client), decisions made in two places (lazy vs eager, structural vs checker diagnostics, two dev servers), last-writer-wins singletons where truth is a per-client set, and TypeScript re-deriving what the Rust core already owns. Same smell as #455 (two walkers decide eligibility), #459 (two paths feed the kept answer), #458.

**How to apply:**
- Third finding on a PR: stop; make a table of the findings, name the root causes, ask 'is one decision made or held in two places?' and 'what is the state machine and who owns it?'.
- Remedy shape: one owner for each decision (prefer the Rust core's merged answer over re-deriving in TS), one explicit reducer (pure state x event -> state x effects), and a model-based/property test of the invariants after quiescence, with the earlier findings as named regression sequences.
- Give such a worker room (cap ~100 calls, Opus); caps suit mechanical work, not stateful mechanisms.
- Before accepting any worker fix ask: is the same fact decided or held anywhere else?

**Second instance, 2026-11-15 (#467, tsrs_module swapped for oxc_resolver):** five findings in five rounds, each in glue code that re-created an old behaviour (symlink canonicalization, `.cts` conditions, relative tsconfig, fingerprint inputs, a `baseUrl` fallback that guessed which rule answered from whether the path contained `node_modules`). I called the root cause settled twice and was wrong twice. The user: "How are you not guarding against these coming up???"

**Why:** a behaviour-preserving library swap was gated by a single-run identity diff on two fixtures, which cannot see cross-run cache staleness or inputs the fixtures lack; fix rounds added new heuristic code that nothing exercised; the Entire reviewer was the first real review. The swap's premise ("same results, less code") was false: tsrs follows TypeScript 7 (no `baseUrl` for bare specifiers) where the old resolver followed TypeScript 6, and the PR grew to +768/-222.

**How to apply:**
- Before a swap: inventory every behaviour of the replaced component that the code relies on (options, conditions, symlinks, config inheritance, cache keys) and diff old against new over the cross-product, not two fixtures.
- Before pushing any worker branch: read the diff myself for heuristics (a rule inferred from path shape, a guess) and run `/code-review` on it; do not let the Entire reviewer be the first review.
- At the third finding re-test the premise (does the swap still delete more than it adds?), not only the root cause; if not, close the PR.

**Third instance, 2026-11-15 (about 50 findings across trails 404/405):** the user said "consider all of the findings together, architecturally and semantically ... make sure the agents won't find even more things". Eight root classes (silence read as evidence, lossy model asserting exactness, spelling instead of binding, derived state outside the dependency model, one decision with two owners, host assumptions, hand-tuned policy with no reference model, contract drift / fields never populated). Table: ~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/shrink/findings-synthesis.md.

**Why:** guards were DENY-lists (enumerate the wrong cases found so far), so each new grammar form (a `[Symbol.iterator]` key) produced the next finding; about 40% of the raw count was the same code repeated in stacked child PRs.

**How to apply:**
- Design guards as ALLOW-lists: a closed set of proven forms, everything else Unknown/Declined; exhaustive matches, no wildcard arms in decisions.
- Run the pre-push gate in worker-contract.md (invariants, grammar sweep with the checker/TS API as oracle, mutation proof, adversarial pass, then /code-review) before any push; generate tests over the grammar, not over past findings.
- Merge stacks in order and retarget children; do not keep a stack alive across review rounds.

See [[resolve-findings-when-fixed]] and [[worker-token-budget]].
